# Wishweave Level 1 — connected spatial blockout

**BLOCKOUT ONLY.** `level1-connected-layout.glb` is real glTF 2.0 3D geometry: one continuous gently sloping main ribbon, one connected branch/rejoin, and named simple landmark geometry. It still needs approved textured ornamental production art matching the separate loomcity target. It is not a finished game or production scenery asset. There are no image plates, textures, rigged characters, colliders, AI, or controls.

## Files

- `level1-connected-layout.glb` — engine-neutral binary glTF spatial scaffold.
- `route.json` — authoritative centerlines, arc lengths, widths, sections, spawns, collectible positions, branch links, and finish coordinates.
- `course-overhead.svg` — exact X/Z overhead projection of the same route data.
- `validation.json` — generated topology, slope, continuity, mesh, and placement checks.
- `generate_course.py` — deterministic reusable generator; Python 3 and NumPy only.

Run `python generate_course.py --output .` from this directory to regenerate all outputs. The script defaults to its own directory. It overwrites only the listed generated outputs.

## Spatial contract

World units are meters, Y is up, and +Z is forward. Main route is 201.319 m long and 6 m wide; branch is 19.543 m long and 2.6 m wide. All `s` values are dense-reference 3D arc length in meters; summing the exported sample chords differs by less than 4 mm over each complete route. Main samples are at most 0.5 m apart; branch samples at most 0.25 m apart. `points` contain `x`, `y`, `z`, `s`, `width`, `tangent`, and `sectionId`. `y` is deck surface elevation. Interpolate between samples, then apply the controller's own grounded/foot offset. Tangent is unit 3D forward; horizontal right is `normalize([tangent.z, 0, -tangent.x])`.

`mainRoute.spawn` and `spawnPositions.player` are the same ground reference. `mainRoute.finish`, top-level `finish`, the Flowergate node origin, and `Finish_Trigger_Origin` use the same endpoint. The visible finish band extends 1.2 m backward from that endpoint with a tiny render offset. A controller should detect crossing the finish plane or `s >= mainRoute.length`, not proximity to a decorative support.

`branches[0].startS` and `endS` address the main route. Its `points[].s` is local branch distance; `points[].mainS` gives monotonically increasing equivalent main-route progress. The `from` and `to` positions exactly match main samples. `connectivity` explicitly links both junctions. The bypass intentionally overlaps the main deck at fork/rejoin to guarantee connected surface; collision union/baking and engine playtesting remain required. This is not a ready-made production collision mesh.

Six sections divide the same unbroken road; they are metadata ranges, not separate rooms. Landmark solids sit off the 6 m floor; arch/gate crossbars are overhead. The Snagling landing and butterfly banner are location placeholders, not characters or behavior. Collectible markers occur at 15% red, 52% teal, and 80% gold.

## Verification and handoff

Generated checks currently pass: max main slope 2.541°, max branch slope 0.197°, minimum main horizontal bend radius 23.124 m. The main ribbon outline has no self intersections. Mesh indices, nondegenerate faces, finite positions, and unit vertex normals are checked. These are geometric checks; visual fidelity, camera clearance, animation, physics, gameplay and accessibility still require implementation and engine review.

Use named nodes and route anchors to replace blockout masses with approved scenery while preserving the connected floor and all route coordinates. Gate supports leave more than 6 m clear; there are no rails or fall protection in this scaffold. Flat colors indicate object roles and are not final material decisions.

# Wishweave Level 1 — connected spatial blockout

**BLOCKOUT ONLY.** `level1-connected-layout.glb` is real glTF 2.0 3D geometry: one continuous gently sloping main ribbon, one connected branch/rejoin, and named simple landmark geometry. It still needs approved textured ornamental production art matching the separate loomcity target. It is not a finished game or production scenery asset. There are no image plates, textures, rigged characters, colliders, AI, or controls.

## Files

- `level1-connected-layout.glb` — engine-neutral binary glTF spatial scaffold.
- `route.json` — authoritative centerlines, arc lengths, widths, sections, spawns, collectible positions, branch links, and finish coordinates.
- `course-overhead.svg` — exact X/Z overhead projection of the same route data.
- `validation.json` — generated topology, slope, continuity, mesh, and placement checks.
- `generate_course.py` — deterministic reusable generator; Python 3 and NumPy only.

Run `python generate_course.py --output .` from this directory to regenerate all outputs. The script defaults to its own directory. It overwrites only the listed generated outputs.

## Spatial contract

World units are meters, Y is up, and +Z is forward. Main route is 201.319 m long and 6 m wide; branch is 19.543 m long and 2.6 m wide. All `s` values are dense-reference 3D arc length in meters; summing the exported sample chords differs by less than 4 mm over each complete route. Main samples are at most 0.5 m apart; branch samples at most 0.25 m apart. `points` contain `x`, `y`, `z`, `s`, `width`, `tangent`, and `sectionId`. `y` is deck surface elevation. Interpolate between samples, then apply the controller's own grounded/foot offset. Tangent is unit 3D forward; horizontal right is `normalize([tangent.z, 0, -tangent.x])`.

`mainRoute.spawn` and `spawnPositions.player` are the same ground reference. `mainRoute.finish`, top-level `finish`, the Flowergate node origin, and `Finish_Trigger_Origin` use the same endpoint. The visible finish band extends 1.2 m backward from that endpoint with a tiny render offset. A controller should detect crossing the finish plane or `s >= mainRoute.length`, not proximity to a decorative support.

`branches[0].startS` and `endS` address the main route. Its `points[].s` is local branch distance; `points[].mainS` gives monotonically increasing equivalent main-route progress. The `from` and `to` positions exactly match main samples. `connectivity` explicitly links both junctions. The bypass intentionally overlaps the main deck at fork/rejoin to guarantee connected surface; collision union/baking and engine playtesting remain required. This is not a ready-made production collision mesh.

Six sections divide the same unbroken road; they are metadata ranges, not separate rooms. Landmark solids sit off the 6 m floor; arch/gate crossbars are overhead. The Snagling landing and butterfly banner are location placeholders, not characters or behavior. Collectible markers occur at 15% red, 52% teal, and 80% gold.

## Verification and handoff

Generated checks currently pass: max main slope 2.541°, max branch slope 0.197°, minimum main horizontal bend radius 23.124 m. The main ribbon outline has no self intersections. Mesh indices, nondegenerate faces, finite positions, and unit vertex normals are checked. These are geometric checks; visual fidelity, camera clearance, animation, physics, gameplay and accessibility still require implementation and engine review.

Use named nodes and route anchors to replace blockout masses with approved scenery while preserving the connected floor and all route coordinates. Gate supports leave more than 6 m clear; there are no rails or fall protection in this scaffold. Flat colors indicate object roles and are not final material decisions.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds the Wishweave Wonders Level 1 debug APK from android/ (which packages ../game).
#
#   tools/build-android.sh [--allow-incomplete-game] [extra gradle args...]
#
# Environment (all optional):
#   ANDROID_HOME   Android SDK (default /opt/android-sdk; needs platforms;android-36, build-tools;35.0.0)
#   GRADLE_BIN     Gradle used ONLY to create the wrapper when it is missing (default /opt/gradle/bin/gradle,
#                  then `gradle` on PATH). The build itself always runs through ./gradlew (Gradle 8.13).
#   JAVA_HOME      JDK 17+ with javac (the system default is used otherwise)
#
# Output: dist/wishweave-wonders-level1-debug.apk (+ .sha256), debug-signed with the local debug keystore.
set -euo pipefail

GRADLE_VERSION=8.13
# Official SHA-256 of gradle-8.13-bin.zip (https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-8.13-bin.zip.sha256);
# written into gradle-wrapper.properties so the wrapper verifies the download.
GRADLE_DIST_SHA256=20f1b1176237254a6fc204d8434196fa11a4cfb387567519c61556e8710aed78

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
ANDROID_DIR="$REPO/android"
DIST_DIR="$REPO/dist"
APK_SRC="$ANDROID_DIR/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk"
APK_OUT="$DIST_DIR/wishweave-wonders-level1-debug.apk"

ALLOW_INCOMPLETE=0
GRADLE_ARGS=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --allow-incomplete-game) ALLOW_INCOMPLETE=1 ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,13p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) GRADLE_ARGS+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done
if [ "$ALLOW_INCOMPLETE" = 1 ]; then
  GRADLE_ARGS+=("-Pwishweave.allowIncompleteGame=true")
fi

log() { printf '\n== %s\n' "$*"; }
die() { printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- SDK + JDK
export ANDROID_HOME="${ANDROID_HOME:-/opt/android-sdk}"
export ANDROID_SDK_ROOT="$ANDROID_HOME"
[ -d "$ANDROID_HOME/platforms/android-36" ] || die "Android SDK platform 36 not found under $ANDROID_HOME (set ANDROID_HOME)."
[ -d "$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/35.0.0" ] || echo "WARNING: build-tools 35.0.0 not found under $ANDROID_HOME; Gradle may try to install it."

JAVA_CMD="java"; JAVAC_CMD="javac"
if [ -n "${JAVA_HOME:-}" ]; then JAVA_CMD="$JAVA_HOME/bin/java"; JAVAC_CMD="$JAVA_HOME/bin/javac"; fi
command -v "$JAVAC_CMD" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "javac not found: a full JDK 17+ is required (set JAVA_HOME)."
JAVA_MAJOR="$("$JAVA_CMD" -XshowSettings:properties -version 2>&1 | awk -F'= ' '/java.specification.version/ {print $2; exit}')"
JAVA_MAJOR="${JAVA_MAJOR#1.}"
[ -n "$JAVA_MAJOR" ] && [ "$JAVA_MAJOR" -ge 17 ] 2>/dev/null || die "JDK 17+ required (found: ${JAVA_MAJOR:-unknown})."
echo "JDK $JAVA_MAJOR ($(command -v "$JAVA_CMD")), ANDROID_HOME=$ANDROID_HOME"

[ -f "$REPO/game/index.html" ] || {
  [ "$ALLOW_INCOMPLETE" = 1 ] || die "game/index.html is missing. Finish game/ first, or pass --allow-incomplete-game for a host-only test build."
  echo "WARNING: game/index.html is missing; building a host-only test APK (--allow-incomplete-game)."
}

plugins {
    id 'com.android.application' version '8.13.2' apply false
}
// Google's public mirror of Maven Central is listed before Maven Central: repo.maven.apache.org rate-limits
// (HTTP 429) some shared/cloud networks, including the one this project was built on. Maven Central stays as
// the fallback, so builds elsewhere are unaffected.
pluginManagement {
    repositories {
        google()
        maven { url 'https://maven-central.storage-download.googleapis.com/maven2/' }
        mavenCentral()
        gradlePluginPortal()
    }
}
dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositoriesMode.set(RepositoriesMode.FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS)
    repositories {
        google()
        maven { url 'https://maven-central.storage-download.googleapis.com/maven2/' }
        mavenCentral()
    }
}
rootProject.name = 'WishweaveWondersLevel1'
include ':app'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Continuously save the whole project to GitHub.
#
#   tools/autosave.sh [interval-seconds] [history-every-n-cycles]
#
# Every interval (default 3 s) it commits any change in the repository and pushes
# the current branch; every n-th cycle (default 5, i.e. about every 15 s) it first
# refreshes history/ (chat + agent transcripts) with tools/export-history.py.
# A lock file keeps it from colliding with manual commits that use the same lock:
#   ( flock 9; git ... ) 9>.git/autosave.lock
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
INTERVAL=${1:-3}
HIST_EVERY=${2:-5}
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
n=0
while true; do
  if (( n % HIST_EVERY == 0 )); then
    python3 -I tools/export-history.py >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "history export failed $(date -u +%T)"
  fi
  n=$((n + 1))
  (
    flock -w 120 9 || exit 0
    if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
      changed=$(git status --porcelain | wc -l)
      git add -A >/dev/null 2>&1
      git -c user.name="Claude" -c user.email="noreply@anthropic.com" commit -q -m "Auto-save $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ): ${changed} changed paths

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RPbwyzH3cusTNJXb1jR8a5" || echo "commit failed $(date -u +%T)"
    fi
    ahead=$(git rev-list --count "@{u}..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
    if [ "$ahead" != "0" ]; then
      for i in 1 2 3 4; do
        if git push -q -u origin "$BRANCH" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "pushed $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) at $(date -u +%T)"
          break
        fi
        sleep $((2 ** i))
      done
    fi
  ) 9>.git/autosave.lock
  sleep "$INTERVAL"
done

# Wishweave Wonders — Connected World, Milestone 1 (continue from handoff)

## Context

On 2026-10-16 (18:37 UTC) the user redirected the project: replace the picture-to-picture "plates" (blurred pillar wipe at 0:36–0:37 of 6746.mp4) with **one continuous 3D course** that Purl and Loop physically run along. The user's prompt (`kit/connected/CLAUDIA-PROMPT-as-uploaded.txt`) says: inspect first, explain renderer scope + reuse plan, build **only the connected opening through the next area**, then **stop for review**. The previous session vendored three.js r147 and ran a 4-agent inspection; 2 reports finished (engine, kit code — saved in `history/transcripts/131a49c9-…/subagents/workflows/wf_ab6d9c83-f3e/journal.jsonl`). The plan doc and Milestone 1 were not started.

New user requirement (this message): **every time I fix a screen, notify them and show what I fixed** (real screenshots/clips from the running game, before → after), so they can confirm it's accurate.

State verified: branch `ccr-41c3f304-c2djh7` == old `ccr-207f431c-z9upqo` @ `e7e1fb9`; plate version recoverable at `635b772`. Headless Chromium has WebGL2 (SwiftShader). Android SDK is **not** installed in this container (reinstall needed). Node 22, ffmpeg, Playwright, PIL/numpy present.

### Root cause (evidenced by the engine inspection)
Connector segments in `game/src/data/level.js` have no geometry (`race.js:50` `path:null`); `renderer.js:drawTransitionScene` (406-441) sweeps a blurred plate column (`columnCanvas` blur at :463) and draws Purl in screen space with no floor. The 2D camera (`camera.js`) is scale+translate inside one painting — it cannot turn, so the plate renderer cannot be extended; a 3D renderer is required.

## How I'll show my work (validation protocol)

After each step below that changes what's on screen, I **send the user images from the actual running game** (SendUserFile, rendered inline) with a 2–3 line caption: what changed, how it was checked, anything still off. Images are also committed under `docs/checkpoints/connected/` so they are on GitHub.

| # | Checkpoint | What I send |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Before | Current game frame of the blurred-pillar wipe (the bug) + plan summary |
| 1 | 3D road + camera | Start and tower-bend frames next to target 01 / 02 |
| 2 | Purl & Loop models + run | Frame strip: idle, contact, push-off, swing, landing, jump, brake (both racers) |
| 3 | Controls | Stills/short clips: steer L/R, jump, brake → Loop passes → resume, pause |
| 4 | Branch/rejoin + next area | Normal + debug-geometry stills at fork, side loop, rejoin, Snagling Landing entry |
| 5 | Milestone proof | Uncut MP4s (normal + debug) from one commit at 720×1602 and a narrower viewport, comparison sheet vs targets, APK, commit hash, honest gap list |

If something looks wrong in a checkpoint, I fix it and re-send before moving on.

## Milestone 1 scope

Playable from the opened rug at s=2 m: Spoolwake Pier → Bellspindle Bend around the tower → Tassel Switch with the side-loop branch/rejoin (main s 81.4–97.4) → entering Snagling Landing (~s 112). Fully dressed through that point.
- **The rest of the road is drivable but undressed:** the whole 201 m road exists because it comes from `route.json`. Beyond ~s 115 it is plainly blockout-dressed, so the build can be run to the flower-gate finish line.
- **Red/teal/gold pickups and the finish rule are live:** three distinct threads plus a real crossing of the finish line.
- **Deferred until after the user's review (stated in the report):**
  - Snagling behaviour, butterfly behaviour and the pull lesson. Their sim modules are kept but not placed on the course.
  - Full dressing past the next area.

Defaults I'm choosing (the user can veto at approval):
- **Characters:** procedural **3D crochet Purl and Loop rigs** in three.js, as the kit prefers. Primitives with canvas-generated stitch textures, and a joint hierarchy for hips, legs, arms and tufts. The 2D sprites remain only for menu portraits.
- **Side loop as the shortcut:** the kit's branch is 3.6 m *longer*. The old approved p02 was a "shortcut", and the prompt asks for "a valid shorter route". So the side loop gets a visible teal **speed ribbon**: +25% speed, which nets out about 0.5 s faster.
- **The road is built from `route.json`:** that is the kit's authoritative contract. The GLB is not loaded at runtime, so `file://` and the APK need no loader. A check tool proves our road matches the GLB's walkable top.

## Implementation steps

**1. Plan doc.** Write `docs/CONNECTED-WORLD-PLAN.md`: the root cause with file:line evidence, a keep/replace table and the renderer scope (from the two finished inspection reports). Send checkpoint 0.

**2. Route data + math (core, testable in Node).**
- `tools/build-route-data.py` turns kit `scenery/route.json` into `game/src/data/route.js` (`WW.ROUTE`). It is compact and records the source sha256.
- `game/src/core/route.js` (`WW.route`) is a port of the kit's `route-motion.mjs` (`sampleRoad`, `advanceRun`) in house style: classic script, no arrows or `?.`. It adds:
  - **Sign fix:** positive lateral = the player's screen-right. The kit's +right renders on screen-left in three.js (verified in the kit-code report).
  - **Route graph:** main road + tassel-bypass, `mainS` progress, `project(worldPos, sHint)`.
  - **Branch handoff:** a world-space fork/rejoin handoff with lateral blending and overflow carry, plus a junction decision window.
- `game/src/core/gesture.js` (`WW.gesture`) is a syntax-only port of the kit's `touch-input.mjs` classifier and gesture machine.
- `tools/check-route-vs-glb.py` parses the GLB `Road_*_Walkable_Top` vertices and reports their maximum deviation from the route-derived deck edges.

**3. Sim on the connected route** (rules kept, plate geometry removed).
- **`data/level.js`:**
  - Keep objectives, stitches and the Loop form.
  - Replace plate/connector `route`/`loopRoute` with course sections and items by `mainS`, taken from `WW.ROUTE.collectibles`.
  - Add the side-loop config and new pacing.
- **`sim/race.js`:**
  - Keep countdown, fixed step, pause, finish/ranks, input dispatch and the debug API.
  - **Delete** connectors, `setTransitionFor`, the transition kinds and `connectorLaneSpacing`.
  - Racer state becomes `{routeId, s, mainS, lateral, latTarget, speed, braked, jump, gaitPhase, heading}`.
  - Steering: a swipe moves `latTarget` by one 1.6 m step, smoothed and clamped to ±(w/2 − bodyRadius).
  - Jump: one arc along road-up.
  - Brake toggle: about 0.22 s decel to idle, then accelerate on resume. A jump while stopped happens in place and does not resume running.
  - Branch: queue a left swipe inside the window before the fork.
  - Finish: `mainS ≥ length` with three distinct threads; each racer is timed independently.
- **`sim/inventory.js`:** locations become `mainS` + lateral; pickup uses world distance. Call `refreshObjective` on collect (fixes the stale objective bug).
- **`sim/loop-ai.js`:** keep the seeded plan. On the route Loop gets:
  - a seeded branch choice with a reaction delay;
  - a seeded stumble as a visible mistake;
  - its own lateral line, steering around Purl when passing;
  - no mirroring of the player's speed and no teleports.

  Loop keeps racing while Purl brakes.
- **`sim/stitches.js` / `sim/snagling.js`:** kept untouched and inert, with no course placements in M1.

**4. 3D renderer** (same public API as `main.js` uses: `createRenderer/resize/render/handleEvents/getTapTargets/getLayout`, plus `worldToScreen(vec3)`).
- **Files:** new modules under `game/src/render/`. The old plate modules (camera, world, setpieces, plate parts of renderer/pull/features) are removed from `index.html` and the tree; they stay recoverable at `635b772`. `game/vendor/three.min.js` gets a script tag.
- **`materials.js`:** canvas-generated crochet textures:
  - red carpet with gold and teal floral motifs, UV along s and across the width;
  - gold braided rope;
  - wood post, knit tower bands, purple tassel yarn;
  - teal tapestry for the banners.
- **`course.js`:**
  - **Road:** the road deck and sides from route samples, the side-loop deck with the teal speed ribbon, and gold rope rails on offset curves.
  - **Roadside props:** posts with tassels and lanterns, Bellspindle and Tassel towers at landmark positions with banners, and the tassel arch.
  - **Backdrop:** a distant city/sky using legacy art only as a far painted cylinder (allowed by the kit), plus clouds and fog.
  - **Collisions:** landmark footprints are checked against the walkable width.
- **`racers.js`:** Purl (coral, one curled tuft) and Loop (teal, two loop ears).
  - **Gait:** driven by distance, with contact, push-off, swing and landing; arms oppose the legs; mild bob and lean; heading follows the route tangent; idle breathing when stopped.
  - **Other states:** jump arc, brake lean, landing squash.
  - **Contact:** a contact shadow on the road normal.
- **`chase.js`:** chase camera behind and above Purl, looking ahead across the route graph.
  - Time-based damping keeps Purl at about 15–20% of screen height.
  - The camera is pulled in when a tower would come between it and Purl.
- **`props.js`:** 3D thread spools with hover/spin, pickup sparkle and a fly-up to the HUD counter (reusing `hudTarget`).
- **`debug.js`:** `?debug=geom` overlay showing:
  - deck edges, clamp lines, the centreline and the branch outline;
  - root-contact crosshairs;
  - landmark footprints.
- **WebGL context lost/restored:** handled.

**5. Input + UI.**
- `ui/touch.js` ports the kit adapter (capture listeners, cancel/second-finger blocking, blur reset; UI elements excluded). It replaces the pointer half of `ui/input.js`; keyboard support is kept.
- Accessible **Left / Right / Jump / Run-Stop** buttons (≥48 dp) go in `index.html`/`style.css`, kept clear of Purl's feet and the rewards strip.
- `main.js` wiring for the buttons.
- HUD progress comes from `mainS`; the How-to-play text is updated.
- The cash-out lock stays.

**6. Tests.**
- **Kit tests ported** to `tests/unit/gesture.test.cjs` and `route.test.cjs` (34 tests), run against the ported classic scripts.
- **New `tests/unit/connected.test.cjs`:**
  - fork/rejoin continuity (no per-step jump);
  - lateral clamp;
  - brake timing, and Loop passing during the brake;
  - jump-in-place without resume;
  - pause freezes everything;
  - pickup updates the counter and objective in the same step;
  - a duplicate type can't stand in for a missing one;
  - finish needs crossing plus three distinct threads;
  - determinism across replays.
- **Existing plate-engine tests:** retarget the surviving rules. Tests of removed mechanics (connectors/wipes/plate events) are deleted with them. Snagling, butterfly and pull tests return in M2. Every one is listed in the report.
- **`tests/e2e/connected.cjs`** replaces `opening.cjs`: a real CDP touch run on a manual clock, with on-screen touch markers in test mode.

**7. Proof + Android.**
- **Recordings:** uncut MP4s from one commit, normal and `?debug=geom`, at CSS 360×801@2x (= 720×1602) and 340×800@2x (narrower). They show:
  - left/right on a straight, the bend and the junction;
  - jump;
  - brake with Loop passing, then resume;
  - a jump while stopped;
  - pause/resume;
  - the opening bend;
  - the branch/rejoin;
  - the entry into Snagling Landing with no wipe.
- **Comparison sheet** of the frames against targets 01 and 02.
- **APK:** reinstall the SDK with the history command (cmdline-tools 13114758; `platforms;android-36`, `build-tools;35.0.0`). The Maven mirror is already in `settings.gradle`. Then `tools/build-android.sh` (extend its verify step for the new scripts) builds `dist/` APK + sha256.
- **Testing claims:** I'll say exactly what was tested: headless Chromium with SwiftShader, no physical device, so SwiftShader frame times are not device performance.

**8. Housekeeping.**
- Update the `Claude-Session` line in `tools/autosave.sh` and restart it; it pushes the current branch.
- Update `docs/HANDOFF.md`, including the new branch name.
- Commit and push to `ccr-41c3f304-c2djh7`.
- Stop for the user's review.

## Verification
- `node --test tests/unit/`: all pass, including the 34 ported kit tests.
- `python3 tools/check-route-vs-glb.py`: max deviation reported, within 2 cm.
- `python3 -m http.server 8100 --bind 127.0.0.1`, then `node tests/e2e/connected.cjs OUT --record` (normal and debug, both viewports) with no page errors.
- Inspect the frames myself before sending them: grounded feet and shadow, no wipe or size reset, Purl at 15–20% of screen height, rails not clipping, towers occluding correctly.
- `tools/build-android.sh` produces the APK, and its verify step lists the new files.

entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

  - **Roadside props:** posts with tassels and lanterns, Bellspindle and Tassel towers at landmark positions with banners, and the tassel arch.
  - **Backdrop:** a distant city/sky using legacy art only as a far painted cylinder (allowed by the kit), plus clouds and fog.
  - **Collisions:** landmark footprints are checked against the walkable width.
- **`racers.js`:** Purl (coral, one curled tuft) and Loop (teal, two loop ears).
  - **Gait:** driven by distance, with contact, push-off, swing and landing; arms oppose the legs; mild bob and lean; heading follows the route tangent; idle breathing when stopped.
  - **Other states:** jump arc, brake lean, landing squash.
  - **Contact:** a contact shadow on the road normal.
- **`chase.js`:** chase camera behind and above Purl, looking ahead across the route graph.
  - Time-based damping keeps Purl at about 15–20% of screen height.

- **`props.js`:** 3D thread spools with hover/spin, pickup sparkle and a fly-up to the HUD counter (reusing `hudTarget`).
- **`debug.js`:** `?debug=geom` overlay showing:

  - root-contact crosshairs;
  - landmark footprints.
- **WebGL context lost/restored:** handled.

**5. Input + UI.**
- `ui/touch.js` ports the kit adapter (capture listeners, cancel/second-finger blocking, blur reset; UI elements excluded). It replaces the pointer half of `ui/input.js`; keyboard support is kept.
- Accessible **Left / Right / Jump / Run-Stop** buttons (≥48 dp) go in `index.html`/`style.css`, kept clear of Purl's feet and the rewards strip.
- `main.js` wiring for the buttons.

- The cash-out lock stays.

- **Kit tests ported** to `tests/unit/gesture.test.cjs` and `route.test.cjs` (34 tests), run against the ported classic scripts.
- **New `tests/unit/connected.test.cjs`:**

  - lateral clamp;
  - brake timing, and Loop passing during the brake;
  - jump-in-place without resume;

  - finish needs crossing plus three distinct threads;
  - determinism across replays.

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskList
entries.description:
Use this tool to list all tasks in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- To see what tasks are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find tasks that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a task, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available task
- **Prefer working on tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones

## Output

Returns a summary of each task:
- **id**: Task identifier (use with TaskGet, TaskUpdate)
- **subject**: Brief description of the task
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Agent ID if assigned, empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open task IDs that must be resolved first (tasks with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use TaskGet with a specific task ID to view full details including description and comments.

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.
